title: Parameter-dependent linear frequency substitution in a compact oscillatory kernel
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] and the symbol and frequency-cutoff conventions of [def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators]. Let $m\geq1$, $p,q\geq0$, $r\in\mathbf Z$, and let $W\subset\mathbf R^m\times\mathbf R^m$ be open. Let $B:W\to\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbf R)$ be smooth and set $F(x,y)=B(x,y)(x-y)$. Suppose $D_yF(x,y)$ is invertible on $W$. Let $b(x,y,\eta)$ be a smooth complex $q\times p$ matrix amplitude on $W\times\mathbf R^m$, vanishing outside a fixed compact subset $C\subset W$ in the spatial variables, and satisfying, for all multi-indices, $$\|\partial_x^\alpha\partial_y^\gamma\partial_\eta^\beta b(x,y,\eta)\|\leq C_{\alpha\gamma\beta}(1+|\eta|)^{r-|\beta|}.$$ Define, on $W$, $$c(x,y,\xi)=\frac{b(x,y,B(x,y)^{-T}\xi)}{|\det B(x,y)|},$$ and extend both amplitudes by zero off $W$. For every $\rho\in C_c^\infty(\mathbf R^m)$ equal to one near zero, the kernels $$K_R^F(x,y)=(2\pi)^{-m}\int e^{iF(x,y)\cdot\eta}b(x,y,\eta)\rho(\eta/R)\,d\eta$$ converge as $R\to\infty$ in the space of matrix-valued distributions on $\mathbf R^{2m}$, independently of $\rho$. This limit equals the distributional limit of $$(2\pi)^{-m}\int e^{i(x-y)\cdot\xi}c(x,y,\xi)\rho(\xi/R)\,d\xi.$$ In particular replacing $\rho(\xi/R)$ in the latter integral by $\rho(B(x,y)^{-T}\xi/R)$ gives the same limit. Equality of kernels also gives equality of their actions and bilinear transposes on compactly supported smooth tests, hence equality of their extensions to all distributions whenever these transposes are continuous test-space maps. The support of every kernel and of its limit is contained in $C$.

source.place: WANTED locally: Part I §3.B, global quantization before Proposition 3.6, printed pp.12–13. Agent-supplied oscillatory change-of-frequency prerequisite. Supplemental source read online: https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf, §3, (3.3)–(3.6), printed pp.6–7, and 3.12–3.14, pp.9–10. The parameter-dependent cutoff assertion is supplied by the agent, not claimed to be proved in these notes.

proof.text: Write $z=(x,y)$ and work entrywise. On $C$, $B,B^{-1}$ and their derivatives are bounded; $|\det B|$ has a positive lower bound. Thus $c$ is smooth after extension by zero, with support in $C$. For $R\geq1$ compare the two old-frequency cutoffs $$h_R^0(z,\eta)=\rho(\eta/R),\qquad h_R^1(z,\eta)=\rho(B(z)^T\eta/R).$$ For each multi-index $\alpha$ their spatial derivatives are bounded independently of $R,\eta$ on $C$. Indeed every differentiated term of $h_R^1$ is a bounded spatial coefficient times a derivative of $\rho$ evaluated at $B^T\eta/R$, times a product of components of $\eta/R$. Wherever that derivative is nonzero, compact support of $\rho$ and uniform invertibility of $B^T$ bound $|\eta|/R$. For fixed $\eta$, both cutoffs are identically one on a neighborhood of $C$ for all sufficiently large $R$, since $\rho=1$ near zero. These facts hold for every choice of $\rho$ in the statement.

source.place: Agent proof of the parameter-dependent frequency substitution prerequisite; supplemental Demailly course §3 (3.3)–(3.6), (3.11), 3.12–3.14 read online. Cutoff comparison supplied explicitly here, not claimed as a theorem of those notes.

proof.text: For a scalar test $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbf R^{2m})$ set $$I_R^j(\eta)=\int_W e^{iF(z)\cdot\eta}b(z,\eta)h_R^j(z,\eta)\phi(z)\,dz,\qquad I(\eta)=\int_W e^{iF(z)\cdot\eta}b(z,\eta)\phi(z)\,dz.$$ The invertible $D_yF$ makes $DF$ surjective, so the compact-submersion estimate applies with $n=2m,k=m,H=F$. The product rule, the amplitude hypothesis and step 1 give $p_N(b(\cdot,\eta)h_R^j\phi)\leq D_N(1+|\eta|)^r p_N(\phi)$, uniformly for $j=0,1,R\geq1$; the same holds without $h_R^j$. Hence $$|I_R^j(\eta)|+|I(\eta)|\leq E_Np_N(\phi)(1+|\eta|)^{r-N}.$$ Choose $N>r+m$. The last frequency power is bounded by a constant times $(1+|\eta|^2)^{-(N-r)/2}$, which is integrable by the cited Euclidean bracket lemma. The majorant lemma therefore makes these frequency integrals absolutely convergent.

source.place: Agent proof of the parameter-dependent frequency substitution prerequisite; supplemental Demailly course §3 (3.3)–(3.6), (3.11), 3.12–3.14 read online. Cutoff comparison supplied explicitly here, not claimed as a theorem of those notes.

proof.text: For fixed $\eta$, step 1 gives $I_R^j(\eta)=I(\eta)$ eventually. Dominated convergence along $R\to+\infty$ (the at-top filter has a countable base), using step 2, gives the common limit $$(2\pi)^{-m}\int I(\eta)\,d\eta.$$ The limit is independent of $j$ and of $\rho$. Finite-cutoff integrands have compact support in $(z,\eta)$, so Fubini identifies their tested kernels with the integrals of $I_R^j$. The bound in step 2, integrated in frequency, gives a constant times $p_N(\phi)$; this proves continuity on each fixed compact test space and hence defines a distribution. It also gives uniform convergence on bounded test sets: both cutoffs equal one on $C\times\{|\eta|\leq T\}$ once $R$ is large, while the integrable tail in step 2 tends to zero as $T\to\infty$, uniformly when $p_N(\phi)$ is bounded. Thus the assertion holds also for the strong distribution topology.

source.place: Agent proof of the parameter-dependent frequency substitution prerequisite; supplemental Demailly course §3 (3.3)–(3.6), (3.11), 3.12–3.14 read online. Cutoff comparison supplied explicitly here, not claimed as a theorem of those notes.

proof.text: For each fixed $z\in W$ and finite $R$, apply the Jacobian formula to $\xi=B(z)^T\eta$. Its absolute Jacobian is $|\det B(z)|$, and $$F(z)\cdot\eta=(x-y)\cdot\xi,\qquad c(z,\xi)\,d\xi=b(z,\eta)\,d\eta.$$ Consequently the standard-cutoff $c$ kernel, tested against $\phi$, equals $(2\pi)^{-m}\int I_R^1(\eta)\,d\eta$. With the cutoff $\rho(B(z)^{-T}\xi/R)$ it instead equals the integral of $I_R^0$. Fubini is legitimate: on the fixed compact spatial support $C$, either cutoff confines frequency to a bounded set for this fixed $R$, and all integrands are smooth there. Off $W$ both integrands vanish. Step 3 proves convergence and equality of the three requested limits.

source.place: Agent proof of the parameter-dependent frequency substitution prerequisite; supplemental Demailly course §3 (3.3)–(3.6), (3.11), 3.12–3.14 read online. Cutoff comparison supplied explicitly here, not claimed as a theorem of those notes.

proof.text: Every finite kernel vanishes off $C$. A test supported in its open complement has $b\phi=0$, so its pairing with the limit in step 3 is zero as well. This proves the support assertion. For compactly supported smooth vector inputs $f(y)$ and dual tests $g(x)$, the matrix kernel is tested against the finite sum of products $g_a(x)f_b(y)$. The equality of kernel distributions therefore gives equality of their actions and bilinear transposes as distribution-valued pairings, with no complex conjugation.

source.place: Agent proof of the parameter-dependent frequency substitution prerequisite; supplemental Demailly course §3 (3.3)–(3.6), (3.11), 3.12–3.14 read online. Cutoff comparison supplied explicitly here, not claimed as a theorem of those notes.

proof.text: If the transposes are continuous maps of smooth compact test spaces as in the statement, their difference at a fixed output test is a smooth compactly supported vector function. Step 5 says that each component pairs to zero against every scalar smooth compact test. The smooth-test separation lemma makes it zero almost everywhere, and the continuous almost-everywhere equality lemma makes it zero pointwise. Hence the two transpose test maps are equal. Their extensions to distributions are equal because for every distribution $u$ and output test $g$ both are defined by $u(T^tg)$. This proves exactly the conditional assertion about all distributions; no test-space continuity was assumed merely from finite-cutoff substitution.

The new node lem-sfb-compact-submersion-phase-estimate is true and only states the result (B1–B4 OK). It is the standard non-stationary-phase estimate: a surjective DH means DH^T is injective, compactness of C times the unit sphere gives a uniform lower bound, and N integrations by parts give the bound with (1+|eta|)^{-N}. I tested it with C empty, N=0, eta=0 and a constant H (which shows surjectivity is needed). Its searches were run and recorded, and Mathlib's decay hits are for linear phases only. Searching the DAG found no duplicate: amplitude-reduction, compact-symbol-frequency-kernel and fixed-support-fourier-lipschitz all differ, and the node is strictly smaller than the item and no clause of it. Steps: step 1 checks the chain rule for rho(B^T eta/R), whose derivatives are bounded because |eta|/R is bounded wherever a derivative of rho is nonzero, and both cutoffs are eventually 1 on C. Step 2 applies the estimate with H=F: D_yF invertible makes DF onto; the symbol bound with beta=0 plus the product rule give (1+|eta|)^{r-N}; and with N>r+m the bracket leaf applies with s=(N-r)/2>m/2. Measurability of I_R^j by continuity in eta is left implicit but is elementary. Step 3 is dominated convergence (Mathlib tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence) entrywise. Fubini applies because the finite cutoffs have compact support in (z,eta). The bound C p_N(phi) makes the limit a distribution, and the ball/tail split gives convergence in the strong topology. Step 4 uses the Jacobian leaf with xi=B(z)^T eta: F.eta=(x-y).xi and c dxi = b deta. The cutoff directions are correct (h^1 is the standard c cutoff, h^0 the B^{-T} cutoff), and the absolute value handles det<0. Step 5 covers support and bilinear actions; step 6 uses smooth-test-ae-separation then continuous-ae-pointwise, and continuity of the transposes is the item's own conditional hypothesis.
